full_judgment:
7. Mr. Abdul Matin Khasru, the learned Advocate for the appellant, has taken us through the HR, evidence on record and the impugned Judgment. 

 27. Mr. Abdul Matin Khasru, the learned Advocate for the appellants, submitted that the Bangladeshi Taka and the gold are not contraband goods and the BDR persons illegally seized those. Furthermore, Headmaster Narayan Banik is the tenant and in possession of the rooms wherefrom an almirah, opened by his wife Suchitra, the Bangladeshi and Indian money was recovered and from their 'Puja Ghar' gold bars were recovered but have not been made accused or witnesses in the case clearly proves the concoction of the prosecution case. He next submitted that the alleged PO is within Comilla town and not on the India- Bangladesh border and the search made by the BDR personals was illegal and not in accordance with law. He also submitted that it is in the evidence that the accused appellant No. 1 Subodh is a businessman and owner of a big cloth shop of the town named Bastraniketan, appellant No. 2 Ratan Ghose @ Dulal is his employee and appellant No. 3 was arrested from amongst the persons assembled around the PO house and there is nothing on record that any incriminating article was recovered from their possession and as such they should be acquitted of the charge. He further submitted that the Magistrate came at the request of PW 13, the BDR Major but admittedly without any search warrant as provided under section 98 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and admittedly no formalities were observed as provided under section 103 CrPC before raid and conducting the search and two persons mentioned in the seizure list were fictitious persons who could not be traced out and referred to the case of Niamat @ Chacha Katta Vs. Summary Military Court No.2 and another reported in 1979 PLD (Lahore) 279 wherein it has been held: 

 "No respectable witnesses of locality attending or witnessing searches and various raids conducted by police-provisions of section 103 having been deliberately violated, recoveries could not be used against petitioners in circumstances. " 

 "Where the failure to comply with the provisions of section 103 leave the evidence in an unsatisfactory condition, so that there is reasonable doubt as to whether the offending articles were really in the possession of the accused, the conviction ought not to be sustained" 

 "Search should be conducted in the manner provided in section 103 of the Code of Criminal Procedure." 

 "In the absence of any compelling or substantial reason the provision of section 103 of the Code of Criminal Procedure must be complied with while conducting a search." 

 "The learned Advocate also referred the case of Muhammad Khan Vs. Dost Muhammad and 17 others, reported in 1975 PLD (SC) 607, 609. Though the facts of the case are quite different but the principles laid down therein by their Lordships that" Provisions of section 103 CrPC no doubt mandatory and designed to guard against possible chicanery and concoction." 

 28. Mr. AQ Rashid Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the State, finds it difficult to support the conviction and sentence passed upon the accused appellants and frankly submitted that no formalities were observed during raid and conducting the search as provided under sections 98 and 103 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 29. Considering the evidence on record and hearing the submissions of the learned Advocates of both sides, we find that Bangladeshi Taka and Gold Bars are not contraband articles. Contraband is Indian Rupee which admittedly was recovered from the almirah from the room of Narayan Banik and the almirah was opened by his wife Suchitra but none of them has been made accused in the case for the reasons best known to the informant party and the police. There is also vital contradiction on the point of alleged seizure of the gold bars. PW 1 stated that he recovered it from the belt of a sofa but PW 12 Magistrate Asadul Islam stated that one Captain wadud recovered the gold bars from the 'Puja Ghar" and it is curious enough this important witness of recovery namely, Captain Wadud, has not been examined in the case nor he has been cited as a witness in the charge sheet and no explanation has been given by the prosecution for withholding him. Furthermore, PW 13 BDR Major stated that at the time of search himself and PW 12 Magistrate were sitting in the drawing room and did not see the recovery. 

 30. The provisions of section 103 CrPC are designed to create a safeguard against possible chicanery and concoction on the part of the investigating officer and it is obligatory on the officer about to execute a search warrant to call on and get two or more respectable inhabitants of the locality to witness the search to ensure that the search was conducted honestly. From the evidence of the PWs it appears that many people assembled around the PO house and none was allowed to enter the house but contradicting them only PW 1 stated that in presence of 4/5 respectable persons the search was conducted and two amongst them are seizure list witnesses. From the evidence of PW 14 the Investigating Officer we find that he could not trace out those two persons alleged to be the attesting witnesses in the seizure list and furthermore Chairman Pourashava also issued a certificate that no such persons are inhabitants of the locality and seems to us that they were fictitious persons named falsely. Furthermore, PW 12 the Magistrate himself did not put any signature in the seizure list. Admittedly there was no search warrant issued by the competent authority and it is not understood how PW 12 the Magistrate accompanied the BDR personnel’s to the alleged PO house and under what authority and furthermore, admittedly no formalities have been observed as provided under the law, so we hold that the raid and search conducted by BDR personnel’s were absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 31. From the evidence on record we find no incriminating articles were recovered from the possession of the accused appellants, rather, it is in the evidence of PWs 1 and 14 that the accused appellant Nos. 1 and 2 are established businessmen and they are the owners of a big shop named 'Bastraniketan'. It is also in the evidence that the accused appellants claimed the Bangladeshi taka as their own business money and the search party took away Taka 17 lacs but disclosed less as Tk. 13,95,798.00 and the PW 11 Customs Inspector categorically stated that Tk. 754.00 less was deposited than what was mentioned in the carbon copy of the seizure list which was admittedly prepared at BDR Head Quarter at Kotbari, not at the PO house. From the evidence we also find that co-accused Jashim, since acquitted, was brought by the BDR personnel’s from Kotbari wearing BDR uniform having his eyes and hands in binding condition and the wife of PW 13 also came to the PO house for the reasons not explained by the prosecution. During examination of the accused appellants under section 342 CrPC appellant No. 1 Subodh submitted a written reply giving vivid description about the highhandedness of the BDR personnel’s which the learned trial Court failed to consider along with other evidence on record. These facts in the evidence on record lend support to defence version of the case that they have been implicated in a concocted case at the instance of their rival businessmen. 

 32. In view of the discussions made above and on consideration of the facts, circumstances and evidence on record and also the decisions referred above we hold that the prosecution failed to prove its case beyond doubt and the accused appellants are entitled to acquittal.
